headline: Birds flying south, a café job and a violin on a train
teaser: Why do millions of birds fly south every autumn? What does Mia do at her aunt's café? And who left an old black case on Kenji's train?

articles.title: Why Do Birds Fly South?
articles.dek: Every autumn, millions of birds start a very long trip. Why do they go, and how do they find the way?

sources.name: American Bird Conservancy: How do birds navigate during migration?
Audubon: Five incredible ways birds change their bodies for migration

paras: Every autumn, millions of birds leave their homes in the north. They fly south for hundreds or even thousands of kilometres. In spring, they come back again. This long trip is called migration. But why do birds do it? And how do they find the way?

The main reason is food. Many birds eat insects, fruit or seeds. In the north, the winter is long and cold. If a bird stays there, it won't find enough insects to eat. Snow covers the seeds, and the lakes freeze. So the birds fly to warmer places. There is more food there.

Before the trip, birds eat a lot. Some birds eat about three times more food than usual. Their bodies keep the extra food as fat. Fat is the fuel for the long flight. It gives the birds energy. If a bird doesn't eat enough before it leaves, it will get tired and weak on the way.

How do birds find the way? They don't have maps or phones, but they have other help. Some birds look for rivers and mountains. Many small birds fly at night, so they use the stars. Birds can also feel the Earth's magnetic field. It works like a compass inside their bodies. If clouds hide the stars, the birds will use the magnetic field.

Which bird makes the longest trip? It is the Arctic tern. This small seabird lays its eggs in the far north. Then it flies all the way to the Antarctic and back again. Every year, it travels about 70,000 kilometres. That is almost two times around the Earth!

Young birds often make their first trip without their parents. They seem to know the right direction from the day they are born. Scientists still have a lot of questions about this. If you look up at the sky in autumn, you will probably see a big group of birds. Where are they going for the winter?

articles.title: Saturdays at Aunt Rosa's Café
articles.dek: Mia has got her first job. Her friend Jack in Canada has got a job too, with a very big dog!
paras: Mia is fourteen. Her best friend Jack moved to Canada last year, but they often send emails. Read their emails about Mia's new weekend job.

Hi Jack, Guess what? I've got a Saturday job! I'm helping at my aunt's café in the town centre. I wanted to earn some money for a new bike, so I decided to ask her. She said yes! I start at nine and finish at one. I don't get much money, but I enjoy working there.

My first job every morning is washing the cups and plates. I don't mind doing it, because Aunt Rosa plays music in the kitchen. Then I help at the counter. At first I was nervous about talking to customers. Now I love to chat with them. An old man called Mr Patel comes every Saturday. He always orders tea and a cheese sandwich. Love, Mia

Hi Mia, That's great! I'd like to have a job too, but my mum says I'm too young for a job in a shop. She wants me to finish school first. So I help my neighbour instead. Mrs Brown is eighty, and she can't walk very far. I walk her dog, Max, after school every day.

Max is very big, and he loves running. Last week he saw a cat and started to pull. I fell over in the snow! Mrs Brown laughed, and then she gave me a hot drink. Do you get any free food at the café? And what do you want to learn next? Jack

Hi Jack, Poor you! I hope Max is a good dog now. Yes, I get a free hot chocolate and sometimes a cake. And next month, Aunt Rosa is going to teach me to make cakes. I can't wait to try! Maybe one day I'll open my own café. Then you can come and visit. Love, Mia

articles.title: The Black Case on the Train
articles.dek: A man runs off the train and leaves something important behind. What can Kenji do?
paras: Kenji was thirteen. Every Sunday, he took the train to his grandmother's village. It was a slow train which stopped at every small station. Kenji liked it, because he could read or look out of the window.

That Sunday, a man with grey hair sat opposite him. He had a black case which looked very old. The man was talking on his phone. He seemed worried and in a hurry. At Green Hill station, he jumped up and ran out of the train. The doors closed behind him.
Then Kenji saw the black case. It was still under the seat! He looked out of the window, but the train was already moving. "Oh no," he thought. "What can I do?"

Kenji found the conductor, who was checking tickets in the next carriage. She was a tall woman with a friendly smile. Kenji showed her the case. She opened it carefully. Inside, there was a beautiful violin and a ticket for a concert that evening.

"He's a musician who needs his violin tonight!" said Kenji. The conductor phoned the station at Green Hill. The man was there, and he was very worried. "Please tell him not to worry," said the conductor. "We'll leave the case at the next station. He can take a taxi there."

A week later, a letter arrived at Kenji's house. It was from the man, Mr Lewis. "Thank you for finding the violin that my father gave me," he wrote. There were two tickets in the letter too. They were for his next concert.

On Saturday, Kenji went to the concert with his grandmother. The music was wonderful. At the end, Mr Lewis said, "This song is for the boy who saved my violin." Kenji's face went red, but he smiled all evening.

Kenji found the conductor, who was checking tickets in the next carriage.
"Thank you for finding the violin that my father gave me," he wrote.
"This song is for the boy who saved my violin."

items.q: The bus ___ goes to the airport leaves every hour.
items.why: A bus is a thing, so use which.

items.q: Do you know the girl ___ is sitting next to the driver?
items.why: The girl is a person, so use who.

items.q: A pilot is a person ___ flies a plane.
items.why: A pilot is a person, so use who or that.

items.q: This is the bike ___ my uncle gave me.
items.why: A bike is a thing, so use which or that.

items.q: The man who ___ his bag on the bus yesterday is my teacher.
items.why: Mixed: yesterday is the past, so use the past simple left.

items.q: I like trains that ___ fast and quiet.
items.why: Trains is plural, so the verb after that is are.

kps.fact: Kenji took a slow train to his grandmother's village every Sunday.
kps.q: Where did Kenji go every Sunday?

kps.fact: A man in a hurry left his black case under the seat.
kps.q: What did the man leave on the train?

kps.fact: Kenji gave the case to the conductor, and she phoned the station.
kps.q: Who did Kenji ask for help?

kps.fact: Inside the case, there was a violin and a concert ticket.
Mr Lewis sent Kenji two concert tickets and played a song for him.
kps.q: What did Mr Lewis send Kenji?

summary.intro: Choose the three sentences that tell the main ideas of the story.
summary.model: A man left his violin on the train, but Kenji found it. The conductor helped, so the man got his violin back and thanked Kenji.

options.t: A man in a hurry left his violin case on the train.
options.why: This is the problem in paragraphs 2 and 3.
options.evidence: It was still under the seat!

options.t: Kenji and the conductor helped the man get it back.
options.why: This is the main idea of paragraphs 4 and 5.
options.evidence: The conductor phoned the station at Green Hill.

options.t: The musician thanked Kenji with tickets and a song.
options.why: This is the happy ending in paragraphs 6 and 7.
options.evidence: "This song is for the boy who saved my violin."

options.t: The conductor was a tall woman with a friendly smile.
options.why: True, but it is only a small detail.
options.evidence: She was a tall woman with a friendly smile.
